subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the full-mode registration guard is fixed, should OpenClaw accept `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`, its packaged executor binaries, `node-pty` build surface, and the SDK's argv-carried base64 config transport for this prerelease official sandbox plugin?
rationale: The code guard is mechanically repairable, but accepting a new native sandbox backend dependency and preview SDK transport is a security/ownership decision that automation cannot safely make.

options.title: Fix guard, then require secops approval
options.body: Land only after the non-full registration side effect is fixed and secops explicitly approves the exact-head dependency graph and argv transport boundary.

options.title: Accept the preview boundary as-is
options.body: Maintainers may approve the native dependency and argv transport after manual review, owning the preview-SDK risk for this official external plugin.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport change
options.body: Hold or close the PR until the MXC SDK can pass config through a non-argv mechanism or a narrower package boundary is available.

recommendation.title: Fix guard, then require secops approval
recommendation.body: Land only after the non-full registration side effect is fixed and secops explicitly approves the exact-head dependency graph and argv transport boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS routes the changed sandbox, lockfile, shrinkwrap, and dependency-guard surfaces to secops.
